extracted.intended_audience: ORR staff, referring Federal agencies (e.g., DHS), care provider facilities, child welfare practitioners, and stakeholders commenting on proposed ORR placement/care standards
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance describing criteria, processes, facility types, timelines, and information requirements that ORR proposes to use when receiving referrals and placing unaccompanied children in care provider facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity and respect in all placements
rubrics_metrics.description: For all placements, unaccompanied children shall be treated with dignity, respect, and special concern for their particular vulnerability as unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This principle is based on ORR's statutory duties and is consistent with paragraph 11 of the FSA and current ORR policies; it informs how ORR and care provider facilities should approach day-to-day interactions and decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe and sanitary facilities consistent with vulnerability
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall hold unaccompanied children in facilities that are safe and sanitary and that are consistent with ORR's concern for the particular vulnerability of unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is aligned with the FSA requirement that minors be held in safe and sanitary facilities; ORR uses the phrase 'particular vulnerability of unaccompanied children' rather than 'minors' to reflect the population served.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individualized, strengths-focused care and services
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan and provide care and services based on the individual needs of and focusing on the strengths of the unaccompanied child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR will assess each child's specific needs to determine required services or treatment (e.g., addressing severe neglect or abuse) and to tailor placement and programming accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Child participation in care decisions (developmentally appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourage unaccompanied children, as developmentally appropriate and in their best interests, to be active participants in ORR's decision-making process relating to their care and placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collaborative approaches enable recognition of each child's needs and strengths and foster empowerment, resilience, and self-efficacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection from traffickers and victimizers; tailored protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Care must be tailored to individualized needs and ensure children are protected from traffickers and other persons seeking to victimize or otherwise engage them in criminal, harmful, or exploitative activity while in ORR custody and upon release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifying this requirement reinforces ORR's commitment to consider each child's individualized needs and take actions to safeguard them from harm, including unscrupulous employers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Least restrictive setting in child's best interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Unaccompanied children must be promptly placed in the least restrictive setting that is in the best interest of the child, with placement considerations including danger to self; danger to the community; and runaway risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is consistent with the TVPRA and FSA; ORR must balance least-restrictive placements with ensuring timely appearance before DHS/immigration courts and the safety of the child and others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation when requesting information or consent
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR shall require consultation with parents, legal guardians, child advocates, and attorneys of record or EOIR-accredited representatives as needed when requesting information or consent from unaccompanied children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation is required 'as needed' to ensure appropriate decisionmaking and protection of the child's interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of ORR legal custody and emergency transfer notification
rubrics_metrics.description: All unaccompanied children placed by ORR remain in ORR legal custody and may be transferred or released only with ORR approval; in an emergency a facility may transfer temporary physical custody prior to ORR approval but must notify ORR as soon as practicable and in all cases within 8 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codifies existing practice that custody begins when ORR assumes physical custody; clarifies emergency transfer notification timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral acceptance process and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR accepts referrals from any Federal department or agency at any time of day, every day, and may seek clarification about referral information; ORR must identify an appropriate placement and notify the referring agency within 24 hours whenever possible and no later than 48 hours, barring exceptional circumstances; ORR accepts transfer consistent with the statutory 72-hour transfer requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These timeframes aim to expedite transfers while allowing for exceptions when necessary; ORR will work with referring agencies and may request additional information in accordance with statutory timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defined exceptional circumstances that extend placement/transfer timeframes
rubrics_metrics.description: Exceptional circumstances that may prevent ORR from timely identifying a placement or accepting transfer include: (1) any court decree or court-approved settlement that requires otherwise; (2) an influx; (3) an emergency (natural disaster, facility fire, civil disturbance); (4) a medical emergency (e.g., viral epidemic/pandemic among group of children); (5) apprehension in a remote location; (6) apprehension of a child the referring agency indicates poses danger to self/others or is charged/convicted/subject of delinquency proceedings and additional info is essential; and (7) an act or event not reasonably foreseen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unavailability of documents will not necessarily prevent prompt transfer. ORR does not include interpreter unavailability or reasonable-person-adult determinations as exceptional circumstances for these timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to request/assess from referring agency for placement decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR requests and assesses extensive background information including: (1) how the referring agency determined the child is an unaccompanied child; (2) health-related information; (3) medication/prescription info and days' supply; (4) biographical/biometric details (name, gender, alien number, DOB, country, entry/apprehension dates/locations, manner of entry, current location); (5) trafficking or crime victim info; (6) whether apprehended with sibling/relative; (7) identifying/contact info for parent/guardian and separation info; (8) final destination and intended contacts if apprehended in transit; (9) runaway risk and indicators; (10) history of violence/criminal/gang involvement, risk to self/others, state court proceedings, probation; (11) Saravia class status/documentation if relevant; (12) any needs affecting care/placement including disability-related services/modifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR relies on this comprehensive information to make safe, appropriate, individualized placement determinations and to comply with statutory/timeframe obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible care provider facility types and OON placements
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may place children in shelters, group homes, individual family homes, heightened supervision facilities, secure facilities (including RTCs), and, under limited circumstances, out-of-network placements (e.g., OON RTCs that meet RTC standards or temporary hospital stays); in times of influx/emergency ORR may use facilities meeting subpart I standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placements must take into account the considerations in §§ 410.1103–410.1109 and 410.1901; ORR may favor transitional and long-term home care but recognizes capacity constraints of moving children out of large congregate care (>25) settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for community-based care / home care placements
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, ORR favors placing children in transitional and long-term home care settings (family/group homes) appropriate to age and individualized needs; ORR is considering a community-based care model that would expand family/group home placements and replace terms 'long-term' and 'transitional' home care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Community-based care is intended as a continuum (basic/therapeutic foster family, supervised independent living) to better serve tender-age, pregnant/parenting children, those with extended stays, or those nearing aging out; components include caregiver supports consistent with state licensing and Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard for caregivers
rubrics_metrics.description: Caregivers (foster parents or designated officials) should exercise the Reasonable and Prudent Parent Standard to make daily decisions on age-appropriate activities that maintain health, safety, and best interests while encouraging emotional and developmental growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard is defined at 42 U.S.C. 675(10)(A) and should guide caregivers' discretionary decisions in community-based or foster settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community integration and services under community-based care
rubrics_metrics.description: Under community-based care, children on extended placements would be eligible to attend local schools, caregivers should support integration into local communities, development of relationships, engagement with local services/activities, independent living skills development (e.g., ages 16+), and proactive permanency planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Placement decisions may include consideration of a child's eligibility for legal relief (e.g., special immigrant juvenile status) in a jurisdiction; public comment is invited on this model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best interest determination factors for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR considers the following factors when evaluating a child's best interest: the child's expressed interests (age/maturity), mental and physical health, wishes of parents/legal guardians, intimacy of relationships (family/siblings/others affecting well-being), adjustment to community, cultural background/primary language, length/lack of stable environment, individualized needs (including disability-related), and the child's development and identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR also evaluates the best interests of other unaccompanied children at the prospective facility; these factors are evaluated together to determine a placement that is least restrictive and appropriate to age and individualized needs while ensuring timely appearance and safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'individualized needs' terminology instead of 'special needs'
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR proposes to use the term 'individualized needs' rather than 'special needs' to avoid confusion and stigma; 'special needs' may imply a limited category or be conflated with disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although 'special needs' appears in the FSA and prior regs, ORR invites comments on continued use; the proposed term is broader and intended to capture any need specific to the individual child.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional placement-relevant factors (broad list)
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent available, ORR may consider additional factors: danger to self/community, runaway risk, trafficking or other safety concerns, age, gender, LGBTQI+ status, disability, any specialized services/treatment required or requested, criminal background, location of potential sponsor and safe/timely release options, behavior, siblings in ORR custody, language access, pregnancy/parenting status, location of apprehension, and length of stay in ORR custody.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is necessary for comprehensive review of background and needs to ensure appropriate and safe placements; includes consideration of specialized services and proximity to providers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health and reproductive healthcare considerations for placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain health status on entry, including need for proximity to medical specialists, reproductive health status (pregnancy/post-partum, birth control, recent procedures, medications), whether child is a victim of a sex crime, and other healthcare needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR relies on referring agency information and documents health status in case management to ensure appropriate placements; see proposed § 410.1307(b) for further policies on medical care access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of information to determine placement
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR may utilize information from the referring Federal agency, child assessment tools, interviews, pertinent documentation, and relevant records from local, State, and Federal agencies to determine placements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORR is clarifying its authority to obtain a broad range of information to inform whether a restrictive placement is necessary and to support individualized placement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly review requirement for restrictive placements
rubrics_metrics.description: All restrictive placements (not only secure placements) must be reviewed at least every thirty days to determine if such placements remain warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This codifies ORR's existing policy and exceeds the statutory minimum (which requires monthly review only for secure placements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic placement efforts to facilitate transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: ORR will make reasonable efforts to provide placements in geographical areas where DHS encounters the majority of unaccompanied children to facilitate orderly and expeditious transfers from DHS border facilities to ORR care provider facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement reflects paragraph 6 of the FSA and is balanced against other placement considerations in §§ 410.1103(a) and (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Care provider facility obligation to accept ORR placements and limited denial reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Care provider facilities must accept all unaccompanied children placed by ORR except for limited circumstances: (1) lack of available bed space; (2) placement would conflict with state/local licensing rules; (3) initial placement involves an unaccompanied child with a significant physical or mental illness for which the referring agency has not provided medical clearance; or (4) for a child with a disability, the facility concludes it cannot meet disability-related needs without fundamentally altering its program even with reasonable modifications and additional ORR support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a facility wishes to deny placement it must submit a written request to ORR providing individualized reasons; ORR approval is required before denial; ORR may follow up to seek solutions to the denial reason.
